desk_read: Yesterday's futures session was defined by aggressive short covering in equity indices alongside broad long liquidation in crude oil. Nasdaq 100 led the equity squeeze with price up 1.10% on heavy volume at 1.1x its 20-day average, while total open interest dropped sharply by -15.4k contracts (-5.3%) as shorts bailed out. WTI Crude Oil saw heavier selling with prices down -1.46% and volume running at 1.4x its 20-day average alongside total open interest falling -7.9k contracts (-0.7%) in a classic long liquidation. Meanwhile, silver bucked the soft metals trend, registering fresh capital inflows with prices up 0.73% and total open interest expanding by +860 contracts (+0.8%) on volume at 1.4x average.
oil_read: WTI CLZ26 fell -1.46% with total open interest down -7.9k contracts (-0.7%) and volume at 1.4x its 20-day average, signaling long liquidation into a backwardated curve where the CLZ26-CLK27 spread was +10.46 $/bbl. Brent (NYMEX) BZF27 declined -0.86% alongside total open interest rising +627 contracts (+0.5%) and volume at 1.1x its 20-day average, indicating new shorts within a backwardated structure where the BZZ26-BZK27 spread was +16.64 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a mildly bearish bias driven by long liquidation on volume 1.4x the 20-day average, while Brent displays a mildly bearish bias from new shorts, both warning of downside trend continuation despite the curve remaining in backwardation. Silver also holds a mildly bullish bias with new longs on volume 1.4x the 20-day average, which supports its current trend. Copper features a mildly bullish bias from new longs, also supporting its trend. Across all markets, the short-term positioning mixes weak liquidations with selective conviction, signaling that while fresh shorts in energy warn of persistent pressure, the lack of uniform participation across asset classes keeps the broader picture fragmented.
